A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LineGraph2Road, with readable main texts, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices. Content can be matched despite reorganization and unresolved appendix references in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original road-extraction experiments on three benchmarks, component ablations, segmentation results, and inference-time measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds overpass-detection results and additional graph-construction and readout analyses.

M1.justification: The SAM backbone, overpass head, Coupled NMS, radius-based candidate graph, line-graph Transformer, training loss, and inference procedure are retained. Expanded preprocessing explanations and relocated Transformer equations do not establish a method change; alternative graph constructions and readouts are experimental controls.

E1.justification: Both versions use City-scale, SpaceNet, and Global-scale and already examine overpasses, occlusions, and diverse global road conditions. The added crossing scores and structural ablations assess retained coverage rather than introducing documented new datasets, domains, or input scenarios.

E2.justification: The headline benchmark comparators remain unchanged. Appendix L extends the original-graph comparison with dot-product, bilinear, and Hadamard-MLP readouts, and adds 8-NN and 16-NN graph-construction comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4.7 introduces crossing bounding boxes, one-to-one matching at IoU 0.25, and pooled TP/FP/FN scoring. Appendices K-L add radius, neighbor-count, and controlled readout configurations. Existing dataset splits, training budgets, main metrics, and inference settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands tests of central design choices: neighborhood-radius sensitivity, alternative original-graph readouts, and radius-based versus K-NN graph construction. It also directly quantifies overpass recovery. The NMS comparison in Section 4.6 already existed in v1 Appendix A.3 and is not a new study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new detection counts and additional score rows do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1-3 retain their scores, but v2 adds substantial results in Table 5 and Appendices K-L, including overpass-detection F1 of 49.70 for Ours with overpass versus 30.55 for SAM-Road with overpass. The existing SAM-Road-with-overpass City-scale F1/APLS changes from 77.40/68.34 in v1 Table 5 to 77.89/66.82 in v2 Table C.1. Table 4 also corrects Coupled NMS F1 from 82.06 to 82.37.

T1.justification: Appendix L.1 adds the line-graph construction complexity bound O(M + sum_v deg(v)^2). The NMS lemma, structural-representation definitions, assumptions, Whitney-based argument, and proofs are otherwise retained; moving Transformer equations into Appendix D does not change their mathematics.

C1.justification: The contribution statement shifts from presenting a novel line-graph Transformer strategy for expressive link representations toward emphasizing an integrated pipeline and empirical validation of established line-graph reasoning. The main road-extraction, overpass-handling, and benchmark-superiority claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 explains limited sampling gains through short candidate edges and the downsampled SAM feature map, and interprets Global-scale performance as a recall-oriented tradeoff. Appendices K-L add explanations concerning neighborhood size, readout confounding, and graph sparsity. Existing failure cases and domain-adaptation limitations are retained.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a promise to release code with stated availability and a repository link. Existing implementation settings and preprocessing algorithms remain documented; the expanded overpass-supervision explanation largely restates material already present in v1's appendix.

R1.justification: v2 more explicitly positions line-graph reasoning as building on prior work. After accounting for the separate appendix bibliography, references to road-map completeness, transformer-based remote-sensing change detection, and TopDiG are removed. The broader related-work framework remains stable.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten around connectivity ambiguity, with further revisions to the conclusion and experimental explanations. Graph construction receives a separate subsection, Transformer equations move to the appendix, and the NMS study moves into the main text. Numerous formerly resolved appendix references become '??', impairing navigation.

P2.justification: v2 adds a challenge montage and dedicated tables for detection, radius sensitivity, readouts, and graph construction. The original connectivity-strategy figure is rearranged and relocated, and the NMS table moves into the main text. Figure B.1 corrects 'SAM Decoder' to 'SAM Encoder'; most existing figures and table formats are retained.

improvement.justification: Direct overpass scoring and the Appendix K-L controls strengthen evidence for the central design choices, particularly by testing alternative explanations for the line-graph advantage. The code-access statement and corrected NMS score also help. These gains are limited by unchanged headline evidence and numerous broken appendix references, which reduce usability.
